title: Canadian Confederation
group: HIST-TOPIC — Overview Anchors (each links to deeper subdomains)
examples: What were the main reasons for Canada joining together?
Who were the most important people in the Confederation?
How did the British government influence the formation of Canada?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the Canadian Confederation. This was when several colonies joined together. It was a big change for the region.
One key motivation was economic growth. The colonies needed a larger market to trade with. A bigger area meant more trade opportunities.
Another motivation was the desire for self-government. The colonies wanted more control over their own laws. They wanted to manage their own affairs more directly.
The threat from the United States was a major concern. The colonies felt they needed a stronger defense together. Unity offered better protection for all.
A key figure was John A Macdonald. He was a major political leader who strongly pushed for union. He helped bring the various colonies together.
Another important person was George-Étienne Cartier. He represented the interests of Quebec strongly. His support was vital for the Confederation to succeed.

faq.q: Why did the colonies feel they needed to join together?
faq.a: They needed to create a larger, stronger economic unit. Joining together offered better protection and a bigger market for trade.
asks: What was the main reason for the Confederation?
Why was unity important at that time?

faq.q: What was the role of the British government?
faq.a: The British government played a role by encouraging the union through acts like the British North America Act. However, the colonies also wanted more control.
asks: Did Britain force them to join?
How much power did Britain keep?

faq.q: Who was the most influential person in the process?
faq.a: John A. Macdonald was a very prominent leader who was instrumental in organizing the union. Other figures like Cartier also played crucial roles.

faq.q: Was the Confederation immediate or gradual?
faq.a: It was a process that built up over time through negotiations. The final act was formalized by the British North America Act.
asks: Did it happen all at once?
What was the timeline for the union?

faq.q: What did 'self-governance' mean for the colonies?
faq.a: It meant having the power to make their own laws and manage their own internal affairs. They wanted less direct control from Britain.
asks: What did they want control over?

facts: The Confederation was a process involving several British North American colonies.
Economic stability and trade were major driving forces for the union.
John A. Macdonald was a leading proponent of Canadian unity.
The desire for self-governance was a key political motivation.

quiz.say: The colonies primarily sought to join together for:

options.show: To join only with the United States.
options.say: To join only with the United States.

quiz.why: A larger unified area provided better trade opportunities and security.

wrong.0: This contradicts the goal of self-governance.
wrong.1: The threat was a motivation, but the goal was internal unity.
wrong.2: While defense was key, economic reasons were equally important.

quiz.say: If a colony wanted more control over its own laws, this desire is best described as:
quiz.why: Self-governance means the ability to rule oneself locally.

wrong.0: Dependency means relying on others for survival.
wrong.1: Occupation implies force, not the political desire for control.
wrong.3: Imperial rule means being controlled by a distant power.

quiz.say: A key figure who strongly advocated for the union was:
quiz.why: He was one of the most visible and persistent leaders pushing for the union.

wrong.1: She was the monarch, but the leaders were the politicians.
wrong.2: While important, Macdonald is often cited as the primary organizer of the movement.
wrong.3: The US was a source of pressure, not a primary organizer of the Confederation.
